title: Continuous null-sequence cocycle and closed-subgroup Baire obstruction
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be an abelian group with a norm $\|\cdot\|:A\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ such that $\|x\|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $\|-x\|=\|x\|$, and $\|x+y\|\leq\max(\|x\|,\|y\|)$; give $A$ the metric topology $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|$, without assuming completeness. Let $T,V$ be nonempty compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and $q:T\to V$ a continuous surjection. Suppose there are distinct $v_k\in V$ and points $t_k^-\ne t_k^+$ of $T$, for $k\geq0$, such that $q^{-1}(v_k)=\{t_k^-,t_k^+\}$ and all other fibres are singletons. In the subspace $R=\{(x,y)\in T^2:q(x)=q(y)\}$, suppose both oriented singletons $\{(t_k^-,t_k^+)\}$ and $\{(t_k^+,t_k^-)\}$ are open and closed. Suppose also that every nonempty open $U\subseteq T$ contains both $t_k^-,t_k^+$ for some $k\geq N$, for every $N\geq0$. Let $H_0\subseteq H_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A$ be additive subgroups (subsets containing zero and closed under differences), closed in $A$, with $A=\bigcup_k H_k$. Let $a_k\in A\setminus H_k$ tend to zero. Define the actual function $f:R\to A$ by
$$f(x,x)=0,\qquad f(t_k^-,t_k^+)=a_k,\qquad f(t_k^+,t_k^-)=-a_k.$$
Then $f$ is continuous, $f(y,z)-f(x,z)+f(x,y)=0$ whenever $q(x)=q(y)=q(z)$, and there is no continuous $g:T\to A$ satisfying $g(y)-g(x)=f(x,y)$ on $R$. These are assertions about functions into $A$ itself, with no completion or closure of the subgroup of differences.

proof.text: The fibre classification makes the displayed function well-defined on all of $R$: a diagonal pair receives zero, and any other pair is precisely one of the two orientations of a unique double fibre. Distinct $v_k$ prevent competing indices, and $t_k^-\ne t_k^+$ separates the two orientations.

source.place: Paragraph (3), motivating analytic auxiliary: agent proof of the null-sequence obstruction, not a claim stated in the blueprint.

proof.text: At an off-diagonal point, its open singleton is a neighbourhood on which $f$ is constant, so $f$ is continuous there. At $(x,x)$, fix $\epsilon>0$ and choose $N$ so that $\|a_k\|<\epsilon$ for every $k\ge N$. Remove from $R$ both oriented singletons for each $k<N$. Their finite union is closed and contains no diagonal point, so its complement is an open neighbourhood of $(x,x)$. On it, $f$ is either zero or $\pm a_k$ with $k\ge N$, hence $d(f(x,x),f(r))<\epsilon$. This is continuity at every diagonal point, directly into $A$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), motivating analytic auxiliary: agent proof of the null-sequence obstruction, not a claim stated in the blueprint.

proof.text: Fix a fibre. On a singleton set $u=0$; on the fibre $\{t_k^-,t_k^+\}$ set $u(t_k^-)=0$ and $u(t_k^+)=a_k$. Checking its four ordered pairs gives $f(s,t)=u(t)-u(s)$, including both diagonal values. Thus for a triple in this fibre the required expression is $(u(z)-u(y))-(u(z)-u(x))+(u(y)-u(x))=0$. These are separate finite calculations; no continuous or global potential is asserted.

source.place: Paragraph (3), motivating analytic auxiliary: agent proof of the null-sequence obstruction, not a claim stated in the blueprint.

proof.text: Suppose a continuous primitive $g$ exists. Set $E_n=g^{-1}(H_n)$. Each $E_n$ is closed: its complement is the inverse image of the open complement of $H_n$. For every $t\in T$, the covering $A=\bigcup_n H_n$ puts $g(t)$ in some $H_n$, so $T=\bigcup_n E_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior] with ambient space $X=T$, whole subspace $Y=T$, countable index set $I=\mathbf N$, and $A_n=E_n$. The whole-subspace topology is the given topology on $T$. Nonemptiness and the Hausdorff property are hypotheses; every point has the compact neighbourhood $T$, giving local compactness. Obtain $j$ with $U=\operatorname{int}_T(E_j)$ nonempty. By the definition of interior, $U$ is open in $T$ and $U\subseteq E_j$.

source.place: Tag 0CQN, lemma-baire-category-locally-compact, closed-cover consequence in lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior.

proof.text: Tail density with $N=j$ gives $k\ge j$ and $t_k^-,t_k^+\in U$. Both $g$-values belong to $H_j$, so their difference belongs to $H_j\subseteq H_k$. The primitive equation on $(t_k^-,t_k^+)$ identifies that difference with $a_k$, contradicting $a_k\notin H_k$. Therefore no continuous primitive exists, as an equality of actual $A$-valued functions.

Live and side-live still have the item as unsplit with no proof. Compared with the earlier head c190affbb677, only step 4 changed: it now names X=Y=T, I=N and A_n=E_n, writes out the pointwise covering argument and derives U open with U ⊆ E_j from the definition of interior. The split_report summary and date were also updated. Not an identical re-push (A6). The statement, stmt_deps, source, blueprint and created fields are identical to live. The delivery adds no new nodes and there is no repair note. Small case: A = ⊕F_p with norm 2^{-min supp}, H_k = span(e_1..e_k), a_k = e_{k+1}. The hypotheses can hold, so the statement is not vacuous. The only citer, lem-sfb-norm-algcl-profinite-cech-exact step 2, uses continuity, f(y,z)-f(x,z)+f(x,y)=0 and the absence of g with g(y)-g(x)=f(x,y), with matching signs. Step 1: distinct v_k and t^- ≠ t^+ make f a function. Step 2: oriented singletons are clopen. At a diagonal point, removing the finitely many singletons with k<N leaves values 0 or ±a_k with k≥N; the norm is symmetric and completeness is not used. Step 3: the fibrewise potential gives f(s,t)=u(t)-u(s) on all four ordered pairs, and the sum telescopes, including for repeated entries and in characteristic 2. Step 4: E_n = g^{-1}(H_n) is closed because H_n is closed, and the E_n cover T. The cited lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior applies: T is nonempty, Hausdorff and compact, hence locally compact, and N is countable. That node is a Mathlib leaf in the same unit. I checked nonempty_interior_of_iUnion_of_closed at Baire/Lemmas.lean:257, BaireSpace.of_t2Space_locallyCompactSpace at LocallyCompactRegular.lean:23, and Stacks 0CQN at topology.tex:2044. Step 5: tail density with N=j gives a_k = g(t^+)-g(t^-) ∈ H_j ⊆ H_k, contradicting a_k ∉ H_k. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are genuinely elementary. There is no SGA citation and no cycle. Compactness of V and total disconnectedness of T and V are unused, which is harmless. No fixes.
